primary_city_decision_block.title: How to evaluate a personal injury lawyer in Dallas, Texas
items: Case type specialization: compare whether each firm can explain experience with claims like yours in Dallas, not just personal injury generally.
Contingency terms: ask for the percentage, litigation-stage changes, case expenses, medical-lien handling, and no-recovery terms in writing.
Trial readiness: ask who prepares the file if negotiations stall and whether the firm can explain filing, discovery, and trial posture without rushing you to sign.
Reviews and reputation: read reviews for communication, fee clarity, and case-update patterns, then verify attorney status through official Texas resources.
Directory use: treat listed firms as a neutral starting point, not a ranking, recommendation, or endorsement.

case_screening_notes: Ask what facts, treatment records, photos, witnesses, or insurance details make a Dallas consultation productive instead of generic.
A strong screening call should explain what is missing, what should be preserved now, and what could weaken the claim if ignored.
Do not treat marketing confidence as proof of case fit; compare how clearly each firm explains liability, damages, and next steps.
fee_structure_notes: For Texas personal injury consultations, compare the written contingency agreement, case expenses, lien handling, what happens if there is no recovery, and whether terms change after litigation begins. This is a Texas fee-review checklist, not a fixed percentage claim.
Ask whether case costs are advanced, when they are deducted, how liens or reimbursements are handled, and what the net-recovery conversation sounds like before you sign.
If two firms quote a similar contingency percentage, the more useful comparison is usually how clearly they explain expenses, deductions, and settlement math.
trial_readiness_notes: Ask who will own the file day to day, when a claim is escalated toward filing, and what trial preparation actually looks like if the insurer refuses to negotiate fairly in Dallas.
Trial posture matters because insurers price risk differently when they believe a firm can prove damages, preserve evidence, and move a case through litigation.
A useful comparison question is whether the firm can explain negotiation strategy, filing thresholds, and communication expectations without rushing you to sign.
local_statute_notes: Deadlines, notice rules, and filing requirements can vary by claim type and defendant in Texas. Verify timing directly with a qualified lawyer or official source before waiting on records, insurer calls, or settlement discussions.
Use official bar, court, and state resources to verify status and deadlines; the page should guide the comparison, but legal timing still needs to be confirmed directly.

Do not treat broad advertising as proof of case-type fit.

attorney_selection_framework.trial_readiness: Ask whether the firm files suit when negotiation stalls, who handles litigation, whether trial counsel is involved, and whether a case like yours might be referred out.
